newsitem.title: UGANDA: Refugees say Zairean rebels take eastern town.
newsitem.headline: Refugees say Zairean rebels take eastern town.

text.p: Zairean rebels captured the east Zairean town of Bunia and Zairean soldiers fled northwards on a rampage of looting, Ugandan military sources and refugees arriving in this border town said on Tuesday.
The military sources said Bunia fell on Monday night after heavy fighting and the Zairean rebels were on Tuesday clearing a few pockets of resistance.
"Bunia has fallen to the Zairean rebels. That's our understanding of the situation," a Ugandan military source said.
Zaireans among some 3,000 refugees who arrived in Kasese from the fighting said the government troops looted Bunia, beat up residents and raped many women before the town fell.
"The Banyamulenge (rebels) have taken over Bunia. Zairean soldiers have fled from the area and we do not known where they have gone," said one refugee who arrived in Kasese on Tuesday.
"We chose to come to Uganda because Zairean soldiers are looting and raping as they flee the Banyamulenge," she added.

Bunia, at 370 km (230 miles) north of the rebel capital Goma, is the northernmost town confirmed to have fallen into rebel hands. They now control towns across a front 550 km (340 miles) long from north to south, parallel with Zaire's eastern borders.
On the northern front, the previous town to fall was Beni, 140 km (90 miles) southwest of Bunia. It fell on Saturday.
Earlier on Tuesday rebel officer Jean Kabongo, special security adviser to rebel leader Laurent Kabila, told Reuters in Goma that his forces had taken Bunia and the town of Walikale.

He said rebels had entered parts of Kisangani, eastern Zaire's largest city, but there has been no independent confirmation of this. Kinshasa says the city, which has a strategic air base, is firmly under government control.
Already Kisangani has suffered from three weeks of sporadic looting as routed Zairean troops returned from the front.
Some of the refugees at Kasese said on Tuesday they heard armed men speaking Ugandan languages inside Zaire but they could not tell if they were regular Ugandan government troops.

The Zairean government says the Ugandans, who are sympathetic to the rebels, have done much of the fighting on the Beni front but Uganda has repeatedly said its only target is Ugandan rebels active on the Zairean border.
Uganda's army commander said on Tuesday that his troops had crossed three km (two miles) into Zaire and "annihilated and dispersed" the Ugandan rebels.
Major-General Mugisha Muntu said his forces acted on the strength of instructions from President Yoweri Museveni that they could go into Zaire if the Ugandan rebels attacked again.
"Uganda can only wait and see how the situation develops (in eastern Zaire)," Muntu told a parliamentary committee in Kampala.
He said Ugandan troops had since returned to their positions. He did not say when Uganda attacked Zaire but Kampala newspapers spoke of attacks from last Wednesday up to the weekend.
Muntu said two army companies -- around 200 men -- took part in the foray into Zaire. They met little resistance.
